title: Indian police rescue 164 foreign nationals from alleged cyber fraud operation near Delhi
date_note: The pages give only their own publication day (27 November 2026); the Peoples Gazette says police issued the statement on Friday, 27 November.
geo_basis: Peoples Gazette places the operation in Noida, a suburb of New Delhi.
summary: Indian police said they rescued 164 foreign nationals, 92 Indonesians and 72 Malaysians, from a cyber fraud operation in a suburb of Delhi, according to AFP (Gulf News) and Reuters (Oman Observer). Police said the people were illegally confined and forced to take part in it. The Peoples Gazette reports one Malaysian national was arrested and a wider network is being investigated.
plain: Police in India say they rescued 164 foreigners, 92 Indonesians and 72 Malaysians, who were held and forced into online fraud near Delhi. One Malaysian was reported arrested.
exec: Police report a forced-labour online fraud operation near Delhi, with 164 people rescued; a wider network is under investigation, per the Peoples Gazette.

sources.name: Gulf News (AFP): India busts scam network, rescues 164 trafficked foreigners
Oman Observer: India rescues dozens from cyber fraud
Peoples Gazette: India rescues 164 Indonesians, Malaysians from cyberfraud network

evidence.quote: Indian police have rescued 164 foreign nationals allegedly trafficked to the country
The victims comprised 92 Indonesians and 72 Malaysians
A total of 92 Indonesians and 72 Malaysians were rescued, Delhi police said.

validation.note: Gulf News (AFP) and Oman Observer (Reuters) each report the rescue and the 92 and 72 figures from the police statement; the Peoples Gazette adds the arrest.
